examples.subject: Your hearing fee query [descriptive subject; original unavailable]
examples.body:
[Paraphrase of a recipient-posted Money Claims Online email; original subject and staff identity unavailable or redacted.]

Dear [recipient],

I am sorry this has happened. I have contacted the court and sent evidence that your hearing fee was paid in time. I have asked for the matter to go to a district judge to consider reinstating the claim and arranging another hearing. I am waiting to hear whether that can be done.

Kind regards
[Staff name redacted]
examples.source_locator: Customer follow-up beginning this is another email from money claims online; first of two quoted replies concerning the hearing-fee query
examples.notes: Public page fetched successfully. Recipient quotes two received MCOL replies and separately quotes local-court correspondence; this example uses the first MCOL reply only. Names and local-court identity omitted. The body is a paraphrase, with generic salutation and closing. Authenticity is unverified. It preserves the distinction between staff referring an administrative problem and a judge deciding whether to reinstate a claim. It does not adopt the Q&A site's legal advice.

examples.subject: Update on your court query [descriptive subject; original unavailable]
examples.body:
[Paraphrase of a second recipient-posted Money Claims Online email; original subject and staff identity unavailable or redacted.]

Good morning,

The court has received our message about your claim being struck out and is investigating. I cannot give you an estimate of when its enquiries will finish. The court will contact you when it has completed them. Please contact us if you need further assistance.

Kind regards
[Staff name redacted]
examples.source_locator: Same customer follow-up; second MCOL reply introduced as a further response after following up a few days later
examples.notes: Public page fetched successfully. This is a distinct reported follow-up email from the same incident as the preceding example, not an independent case. No duration is inferred from the customer's account. Authenticity is unverified. Generic greetings and closing are retained in a labelled paraphrase; names, case identifier, exact dates and local court are omitted. Useful for restrained status wording that makes no promise of an outcome or deadline.

limitations: Three reported emails come from two recipient accounts on a public legal Q&A site; no independently authenticated HMCTS originals or headers were located for these items.
The second and third examples are follow-ups in one incident and must not be treated as evidence of frequency or general service performance.
Only the first body is a short quotation; other bodies are labelled paraphrases. Subjects are descriptive additions.
Historical administrative explanations do not set current court procedure, eligibility, fees, response deadlines or the outcome of any claim.
